answers.q1: Yarn classic (yarn@1.22.22, set in package.json's packageManager field), with Node >=18 (CI uses Node 20.x). The repo is a Yarn workspaces monorepo covering excalidraw-app, packages/* and examples/*. Install dependencies with: yarn install
answers.q2: yarn test:unit --watch=false   (this runs vitest once without watch mode. `yarn test` is an alias for `yarn test:unit`, which starts vitest in watch mode on a TTY. `yarn test:all` also runs types, lint and format checks before the unit tests.)
answers.q3: yarn vitest run packages/element/tests/bounds.test.ts   (equivalent: yarn test:unit --watch=false packages/element/tests/bounds.test.ts)
answers.q4: yarn test:format && yarn test:lint && yarn test:types   (CI's lint.yml runs yarn install, then these three in this order. They expand to: prettier "**/*.{css,scss,json,md,html,yml}" --ignore-path=.eslintignore --list-different, then eslint --max-warnings=0 --ext .js,.ts,.tsx ., then tsc.)
answers.q5: Don't hand-edit these. Build output and dependencies: node_modules/, build/, dist/, dev-dist/, coverage/, public/workbox, packages/excalidraw/types and examples/**/public (all listed in .eslintignore), plus per-package packages/*/dist and packages/*/build. Lockfile: yarn.lock, which yarn manages. I did not check for it, but it is probably in the repo root. Translations: files in packages/excalidraw/locales/ other than en.json are managed through Crowdin (crowdin.yml is in the root). This is from my general knowledge of the project, and I did not open that directory to confirm.

q1.reason: Yarn classic with `yarn install` from the root matches the accept criterion, with no contradictions.

q2.reason: `yarn test:unit --watch=false` is explicitly accepted, and the extra detail about `yarn test` and `yarn test:all` is consistent with the truth.

q3.reason: `yarn vitest run packages/element/tests/bounds.test.ts` matches the accepted command exactly, and the equivalent given is also valid.

q4.reason: `yarn test:format && yarn test:lint && yarn test:types` covers lint and format plus types, matching the CI workflow.

q5.reason: It names yarn.lock, the non-en locale files managed by Crowdin, and build output directories (dist/, build/, dev-dist, packages/excalidraw/types), all of which are accepted and none of which match a reject item. The hedging about not having verified is only a caveat.
